title: Scoped PRD: CMEK/HSM Integration + Adaptive RBAC and SAML SSO Compliance
text:
Scoped PRD: CMEK/HSM Integration + Adaptive RBAC and SAML SSO Compliance

description:
This PRD defines requirements, scope decisions, and acceptance criteria for customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) and optional HSM attestation in Private deployments, combined with SAML SSO-driven adaptive RBAC and hardened audit logging. Goal: enable regulated customers to meet encryption-at-rest and key custody requirements while preserving zero-downtime rollouts and providing clear sign-off criteria for security and compliance teams.

scope:
Implement support for customer-managed keys (CMEK) via AWS KMS/GCP CMEK + optional YubiHSM/CloudHSM integration for key attestations; map SAML identity attributes to fine-grained RBAC roles with attribute-based access controls (ABAC) fallback; extend audit pipeline to append tamper-evident proofs and configurable retention; expose admin console flows for key onboarding, rotation, and emergency key revocation.

out_of_scope:
Managed hosted KMS offering, multi-cloud HSM product development beyond AWS/GCP integrations, third-party HSM appliance procurement guidance.

acceptance_criteria:
SSO/SAML: Customers can configure a SAML IdP that issues assertions mapping to at least three RBAC roles (admin, operator, viewer) and a custom attribute for per-project access; end-to-end test with Okta/OneLogin passes SSO + role mapping and session creation
RBAC: Console and API enforce role checks for key management endpoints (create, rotate, revoke, export-metadata) and serving endpoints; unauthorized requests return 403 with audit log entry
CMEK/KMS: Platform accepts a customer-supplied KMS key ARN or resource and uses envelope encryption for model artifacts and runtime secrets; sample customer import flow documented and validated in staging
HSM attestation: For customers opting into HSM integration, the platform records attestation artifacts (certificate/nonce) and surfaces attestation status in the console; automated test simulates an HSM attestation exchange
Rotation without downtime: Key rotation can be performed with <= 1% additional latency for in-flight requests and no 5xx error increases across the Canaries job run
Audit logs: All privileged operations (key lifecycle, RBAC changes, SSO configuration, emergency revocations) are emitted to the customer audit stream with fields: timestamp, actor_email, actor_id, action, resource_id, request_id; log integrity proof appended daily
Retention and export: Admins can configure retention for audit logs (30/90/365 days) and export a signed bundle for regulatory review
Security review: Feature passes internal security checklist and external SOC/ISO reviewers sign off during release readiness

signoff_checklist:
PM review of requirements - Aisha Patel
Design review: UX copy and console flows - Maria Gomez
Eng architecture review: key-handling, envelope encryption, and HSM interface - Jun Park
Security review: threat model, KMS/HSM integration, key rotation playbook - Security Team (security_review_required=true)
Compliance review: sample audit exports and retention policy - Legal/Compliance
QA: End-to-end test matrix executed (Okta, OneLogin, AWS KMS, CloudHSM simulator) - QA Lead
Docs: Customer-facing onboarding guide, admin runbook, and emergency revocation procedure published
Release engineering: migration steps validated on staging and rollback tested
Customer pilot: 1 pilot customer onboarded and acceptance documented

risks:
Key leakage in transit if envelope encryption is misconfigured; mitigation: strict TLS and mTLS for KMS endpoints and CI tests for key wrapping
Higher latency for small tokenized requests during rotation windows; mitigation: staged rotation and caching strategies
Customer onboarding complexity: mitigate with step-by-step console wizard and templates
Regulatory variance across regions may require per-customer retention policies; mitigation: make retention configurable and surfaced in contracts

open_questions:
Do we require HSM attestation for all CMEK customers or make it opt-in? (recommended: opt-in)
Minimum support matrix: which IdPs must be tested for GA? (Okta, AzureAD, OneLogin recommended)
Should audit logs be immutable on our side or only delivered to customer-controlled sinks?
What SLAs are appropriate for key rotation operations in Dedicated vs Private tiers?

rollout_notes:
Phased rollout: 1) staging-only feature flags and partner pilot; 2) private deployment GA for customers with signed contracts; 3) opt-in console wizard enabled after 2 pilot success signals. Monitor latency, error rates, and audit log delivery for three weeks before wider enablement.

qa_plan:
Matrix with permutations: (IdP: Okta/AzureAD/OneLogin) x (KMS: AWS/GCP) x (HSM: none/cloudhsm/yubihsm) x (RBAC profiles). Automated smoke tests for SSO mapping, key create/rotate/revoke, and audit export. Manual pen-test focused on key-handling flows.
